newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Britain, France agree to freeze Nazi gold.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Britain, France agree to freeze Nazi gold.

text.p: The United States, Britain and France have agreed to freeze distribution of $68 million in gold looted by the Nazis while officials investigate whether some of it came from Holocaust victims, a U.S. official said on Tuesday.

The gold will be frozen until new evidence can be examined that some of it was taken from private citizens sent to Nazi death camps -- including their wedding rings, watches and even the gold from their dental work.

Officials have always maintained that all of 337 metric tons of gold were looted from the central banks of countries occupied by the Nazis during the Second World War, but Jewish groups maintain that new evidence points to between five and 10 percent of the gold coming from private individuals.
U.S. Undersecretary of Commerce Stuart Eizenstat said it will be very difficult to know the whole truth about the origin of the gold because most of the original amount has been disbursed.
"No decisions have been made concerning the final disposition of the gold," Eizenstat told reporters in a telephone conference.

"The United States, the administration the president are deeply committed to seeing that Holocaust victims are given justice to the extent possible. We take very seriously the claims that the remaining gold should be used to compensate victims of the Holocaust," he added.
An official said that studies were being conducted in the United States and Britain to determine whether some of the gold came from Holocaust victims.

Eizenstat said the U.S. report will examine the issue of the gold as well as the U.S. government role in tracking Nazi war assets and efforts after the war to get gold and other assets back and distribute them to looted countries and the victims and survivors of the Holocaust. It is expected to be completed by mid-March, he said.

Elan Steinberg, executive director of the World Jewish Congress, which has been investigating what happened to the assets of Holocaust victims, said documents in the U.S. National Archives point to extensive looting by the Nazis of gold from private citizens.

"We have documents showing that they looted gold coins, medals, medallions, wedding rings, watches, even the gold from the teeth of death camp victims and melted it down in ingots. The Germans did not just stop at Central Banks," he said.
He added that tests done on the extensive hoard of gold found hidden by the Nazis in caves in western Germany after the war showed that between five and 10 percent came from non-monetary sources.

After the war, Britain, France and the United States set up a joint commission to return looted gold to European Central Banks and in 50 years gave back about $4 billion worth of gold. The commission still had $68 million worth of gold to distribute when the freeze was announced.
The gold bars have been stored at the New York Federal Reserve Bank and the Bank of England.
One British source said that under the agreement which set up the Tripartite Gold Commission, the gold goes to countries whose national banks were ransacked during the war.
But he added: "We are now looking to see whether there is any way we can overcome the legal and practical difficulties that distributing gold to individuals may involve."
U.S. officials would like to see the gold used to create a fund to compensate Holocaust survivors.

Ten countries -- Albania, Austria, Belgium, Czechoslovakia, Luxembourg, Greece, Italy, Netherlands, Poland and Yugoslavia -- have claims on the gold. They would have to be part of any decision, along with the United States, France and Britain, on disbursement of the remaining bars.
"We're engaged in consultations with other member countries," Eizenstat said.
